# libjxl / rans_fuzzer

libjxl's own fuzz target `rans_fuzzer` ([source](source/rans_fuzzer.cc), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over libjxl (libjxl/libjxl at aea3a06e).

Checks 2 properties (listed below); the first, an invariant: Every allocation the library made through the harness TrackingMemoryManager was freed by the end of the run (num_allocations==0, allocation map empty, bytes_in_use==0): a leak check on the JxlMemoryManager path that holds without LeakSanitizer.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against libjxl at commit aea3a06e.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- Every allocation the library made through the harness TrackingMemoryManager was freed by the end of the run (num_allocations==0, allocation map empty, bytes_in_use==0): a leak check on the JxlMemoryManager path that holds without LeakSanitizer ([line 78](source/rans_fuzzer.cc#L78)): a trap; confirmed in the binary.

A failed check marked as ending the process contradicts every halts statement below, so a proof of one implies it on every input it covers.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libjxl` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `rans_fuzzer.plain` | 372,072 | `79d80c36bc26e678f8dff51554f696be6560d0ce75d766ecc81fca53c66c73af` |
| ubsan | `rans_fuzzer.ubsan` | 386,776 | `b9fc01e9489b760ff51987b79cc1f8a0da39f8523f0635595dbedd52603846e3` |
| asan | `rans_fuzzer.asan` | 928,056 | `ae03ab2df193b4af15567f7af60c52fa08a33029e481c50dc666d8ca814a46fb` |
| asan-ubsan | `rans_fuzzer.asan-ubsan` | 959,032 | `356d4d8265073de53c9994a25479ca8c1737fad2d2b5d761623a0e722c95b8e3` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
